messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE: Elevated 5xx and connection resets observed for inference-proxy in region-usw2 (az1a). Trigger: 5xx > 4% for 3m. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: i'm on it — pulling up ingress graphs and proxy health.

leo: CloudWatch shows a burst of ENI attach/detach events in az1a starting ~00:02 UTC.

maya: grabbing proxy logs now. seeing tons of upstream ECONNRESET and NLB failing health checks to some backend IPs.

infra-bot: AWS Event: EC2 network interface changes detected for 4 instances in subnet-az1a at 00:03:18 UTC.

oncall-sre: quick impact snapshot: hosted tier ~2.1% errors (transient), dedicated ~6% errors on several model routes, private/VPC-peered customers largely unaffected.

alex: nodes look OK from k8s perspective but the host NIC counters on g5 hosts in az1a show significant tx drops.

maya: proxy tail (snip):
```
[00:03:10] upstream ECONNRESET id=xyz route=inference-usw2a-az1a target=10.10.8.134
[00:03:11] 502 from upstream, retrying
[00:03:12] 504 request timeout after 10s
```

leo: VPC flow logs show SYN retransmits and RSTs to the NLB on ephemeral ports. points at ENI egress queue pressure or NAT gateway problems.

oncall-sre: immediate actions: 1) enable cross-AZ fallback for affected routes, 2) mark suspect instances out of service, 3) open AWS support case, 4) notify CS + customers.

ops-lead: agree. we need to steer traffic to az1b/az1c quickly but preserve session affinity where possible. can proxy apply a cost penalty per zone?

alex: yes — proxy supports zone penalties. i'll push a high penalty for az1a so traffic prefers healthy AZs but still uses az1a if strictly necessary.

maya: applying penalty: 
PATCH /routes/inference/proxy
{"zone_penalty":{"az1a":1000}}

infra-bot: route update accepted and pushed to control plane (6s).

oncall-sre: starting cordon+drain on the 4 suspect g5 nodes. we'll do one at a time to avoid mass capacity loss.

leo: cordon completed on g5-az1a-007. draining pods — expect KV-cache warms and a few cache misses; slight latency bump likely.

customer-success: heads up — two enterprise customers reporting elevated latencies. sending proactive update now.

oncall-sre: opened AWS Support case #1234567890 (high packet drops on ENI, possible host-level rx/tx queue saturation).

alex: host net counters (snippet):
```
RX packets: 1,235,678 errors: 0 dropped: 0 overruns: 0 frame: 0
TX packets: 1,002,342 errors: 0 dropped: 24673 overruns: 0 carrier: 0
```

maya: NLB pool health: az1a subset went from 3/10 healthy -> 0/10 for several model endpoints.

ops-lead: good containment so far. freeze scale-up for az1a so autoscaler doesn't launch new nodes into a troubled AZ — set ASG max to current.

leo: ASG max set to current for az1a; disabled scale-up for 10m.

oncall-sre: routing change applied only for hosted and dedicated tiers that allow zone-fallback. private deployments unchanged.

customer-success: update sent at 00:18 UTC. promised next update at 00:45 UTC. customers asked about data loss — none reported.

infra-bot: AWS Support acknowledged case #1234567890, asked for pcap and enhanced networking logs, investigating NIC firmware and ENI queue metrics.

maya: starting tcpdump on affected host, uploading to s3:/incidents/4943210000/pcap-az1a-node007.pcap.

oncall-sre: after steering, error rates dropped ~6% -> 1.2%. median latency up ~30ms for routed traffic.

alex: doing a rolling restart of qemu processes on affected hosts to clear kernel NIC state (non-destructive). one host at a time.

leo: first restart completed, host rejoined, tx dropped counter reset on that host, health checks passing.

oncall-sre: monitoring 10m after each host. if stable we continue with the remaining hosts. notifying CS with metrics.

customer-success: customers acknowledged improvement and will wait for next update.

oncall-sre: escalation path: if AWS diagnoses hardware NIC failure, we may need cross-AZ evacuation and AZ-level capacity rebalancing. prepping runbook; handing to night oncall if incident persists.

ops-lead: handoff prep. @carmen you're night oncall — i'll transfer incident artifacts (pcap, cloudwatch links, route patch, AWS case).

carmen: ack, i'll take it. handoff ETA 00:46 UTC. please include list of drained/healthy hosts.

oncall-sre: handoff at 00:46 UTC. status: routing penalty active, 2 hosts drained, 1 host rebooted and healthy, AWS Support engaged. next update in 30m or on major change.

infra-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: incident-tracker id INC-2026-0429-4943210000.

carmen: thanks team. i'll monitor overnight and will reopen broad notifications if anything spikes. closing channel for broad alerting until resolved :lock:
